**[85012858 Research lifecycle engine design surfaces](.ticket/tickets/85012858-cbf3-40df-b55e-b82e89f72434/ticket.toml) — the foundational research ticket that everything else in this 19-ticket epic transitively depends on contains *zero research*.** It has exactly two `notes` parts, both handoff stubs (`fc6afa37...`, `2b715f98...`), and the second is the first paragraph copy-pasted with one bolt-on sentence ("Target tickets: ...9e450826-60e1-437f-b236-2c8839e4ab9e" added). No brief, no cited findings, no design surfaces actually surveyed — just a restatement of its own objective, twice. This is the ticket every `next_tickets` call will surface first, and it's an empty box with a bow on it.

It gets worse: **[9e450826 Plan lifecycle engine implementation](.ticket/tickets/9e450826-60e1-437f-b236-2c8839e4ab9e/ticket.toml)'s only part is byte-for-byte the same handoff text as 85012858's second note** (`84062531-...` == `2b715f98-...` content). One handoff blob, pasted into two different ticket IDs, masquerading as both "research" and "planning." The spec (e9c38d24, section "Implementation Workflow and Role Mapping") explicitly requires planning to "convert the brief and binding decision register into target files, acceptance criteria, validation commands, and scope boundaries" — 9e450826 has none of that: no acceptance criteria field, no target files, no scope. Compare this to [7df984eb Inventory and migrate legacy ticket schemas](.ticket/tickets/7df984eb-c96c-4501-98fa-4e88dd28ec4e/ticket.toml), which has a fully fleshed-out objective/requirements/acceptance-criteria/recovered-contract structure spanning five sections. Track 1 — the very first thing a picker will grab — is the least specified ticket in the entire tree, while Track 5 reads like someone actually did their homework. That's a sequencing hazard dressed up as "done."

## Findings, Ordered by Severity

### 1. [SEVERE] Epic depends directly on all 18 descendants instead of just the terminal review ticket
**Evidence**: [8fdfe135 Schema modernization implementation track](.ticket/tickets/8fdfe135-e3b1-4876-b638-24154edcd78d/ticket.toml)'s `depends_on` field lists all 19 non-epic ticket IDs. But the graph is a strict linear chain terminating at [e03eb731 Review schema modernization completion evidence](.ticket/tickets/e03eb731-877a-4498-832f-d1e41526423a/ticket.toml), whose own `depends_on` already closes over every other node transitively (e03eb731 → 3bb41fb2 → 3eae33fb → 2def6b85 → 7df984eb → 9242e574 → d8bd4c53 → 9e7a5f1a → 9e2c1f17 → 5e1e799e → abd3f280 → 9019477b → 0887b8d6 → 1f8e6e6d → d4233399 → 047dffaf → 7ef3f8db → 9e450826 → 85012858).
**Action**: Prune 18 of the 19 epic-level `depends_on` edges, keeping only `8fdfe135 → e03eb731`. Every other node is already reachable through it — the current graph is doing "epic depends on literally everything" as a substitute for "epic depends on its terminal gate," and it buries the actual linear structure under a flat fan-out that any discovery tool has to re-derive by hand.

### 2. [SEVERE] Six cross-track "belt-and-suspenders" edges duplicate the transitive closure mid-chain

|---|---|
| [1f8e6e6d](.ticket/tickets/1f8e6e6d-c8ea-461d-83c9-c26daf0e3cd3/ticket.toml) → [7ef3f8db](.ticket/tickets/7ef3f8db-d4a9-4135-99eb-3c006070a328/ticket.toml) | 1f8e6e6d → d4233399 → 047dffaf → 7ef3f8db |

Sloppy? No — actually *wrong* in the sense of misleading a reviewer into thinking there are more real coupling points than there are. The user asked for exactly this: discovery/sequencing noise, found.

### 4. [MODERATE] Documentation-quality cliff between Track 1 and Tracks 5–6

**Evidence**: 85012858's second note (`2b715f98-...`) and 9e450826's only note (`84062531-...`) are identical text. This isn't a ticket-edge problem but it is exactly the kind of "two tickets, one artifact" duplication the user asked to flag — a copy-paste handoff masquerading as two separate deliverables.
